'''''Punch-Drunk Love''''' is a 2002 American [[Absurdist fiction|absurdist]] [[Romantic comedy|romantic]] [[comedy drama]] film, produced, written and directed by [[Paul Thomas Anderson]]. [[Adam Sandler]] stars as an entrepreneur with social anxiety who falls in love with his sister's co-worker, played by [[Emily Watson]]. The supporting cast includes [[Philip Seymour Hoffman]] and [[Luis Guzmán]].

After working on his third film ''[[Magnolia (film)|Magnolia]]'', Anderson planned to make his next film around 90 minutes, with Sandler in mind as the lead due to Anderson's love for him and his films. It features the video art of [[Jeremy Blake]] in the form of visual interludes.

''Punch-Drunk Love'' was produced by [[Columbia Pictures]], [[Revolution Studios]], [[New Line Cinema]] and Ghoulardi Film Company, and distributed by [[Sony Pictures Motion Picture Group|Sony Pictures Releasing]]. It premiered at the [[2002 Cannes Film Festival]] on May 19, 2002 before being released theatrically in the United States on November 1, 2002.

Despite its box-office disappointment, grossing $24.7 million against its $25 million production budget, ''Punch-Drunk Love'' received positive reviews from critics, with Sandler's performance receiving widespread acclaim, making a launchpad for Sandler to pursue dramatic or unconventional film roles outside of his usual mainstream comedies. A favorite of several prominent filmmakers and actors, it has been included in lists of the [[List of films voted the best|greatest movies]] of the 21st century.

==Plot==
<!-- Per WP:FILMPLOT, plot summary should be between 400 to 700 words. -->
In Los Angeles, Barry Egan is a bachelor who owns a company that markets themed [[toilet plunger]]s and other novelty items. He has seven overbearing sisters who regularly ridicule and emotionally abuse him, and he leads a lonely life punctuated by fits of rage and social anxiety.

One day, Barry witnesses an inexplicable car accident, picks up an abandoned [[pump organ|harmonium]] from the street, and meets Lena Leonard, a co-worker of Elizabeth, one of his sisters. Lena had orchestrated the meeting after seeing him in Elizabeth's family picture at work. Barry attends his sister's birthday party, where they tease him about his sexuality, leading to a violent outburst in which he breaks sliding glass doors. Afterwards, he privately asks one of his brothers-in-law, a dentist, to refer him to a therapist.

At home, Barry calls a [[phone sex line]] to cope with his loneliness. The phone sex operator tries to extort money from him and then sends four henchmen, who are brothers, to collect. This complicates his budding relationship with Lena, as well as his plan to exploit a loophole in a [[Healthy Choice]] promotion and amass a million [[Frequent flyer program|frequent-flyer miles]] by purchasing large quantities of pudding.

When Lena leaves for [[Hawaii]] on a business trip, Barry decides to follow her. He uses his sister to find Lena, who is overjoyed to see him. As the two spend time together, Barry's sister calls Lena, who lies to her about being in contact with him. The romance develops further, leading to Barry's relief from his emotional isolation.

On the return trip, the four brothers ram Barry's car, mildly injuring Lena. After fighting them off with a [[tire iron]], Barry leaves her at the hospital and sets out to end the harassment. He calls the phone sex line back and discovers the "supervisor" is the owner of a mattress store. Barry drives all the way to [[Provo, Utah]], to confront the owner, Dean, face to face. At first trying to intimidate Barry, Dean finds him more intimidating once he learns that he has come all the way from California. They both agree "that's that".

Returning home, Barry visits Lena to explain why the accident happened. He begs for forgiveness, pledging his loyalty and to use his frequent-flyer miles to accompany her on all future business trips after his pudding miles are processed. Lena confesses she was more upset at being left at the hospital, but forgives Barry and they embrace.

==Production==
[[File:Sandler-Anderson-Watson-Hoffman(Cannes2002).jpg|thumb|right|(L to R) Adam Sandler, [[Paul Thomas Anderson]], [[Emily Watson]] and [[Philip Seymour Hoffman]] at the 2002 Cannes Film Festival]]
After the success of ''[[Magnolia (film)|Magnolia]]'', [[Paul Thomas Anderson]] stated that he was determined to make his next film ninety minutes long and stated that he wanted to cast Adam Sandler in this film.<ref name="patterson">{{cite news |last=Patterson |first=John |date=March 10, 2000 |title=''Magnolia'' Maniac |work=[[The Guardian]] |location=London |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2000/mar/10/culture.features |access-date=April 12, 2010 |archive-date=August 27, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120827044550/http://www.guardian.co.uk/film/2000/mar/10/culture.features |url-status=live }}</ref> After establishing his style with his previous films, he wanted to challenge himself within the parameters of a ninety-minute-long [[romantic comedy]].<ref name="CrazyLA">{{Cite web |last=Turan |first=Kenneth |date=May 20, 2002 |title=Crazy for Love |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-may-20-et-turan20-story.html |access-date=April 25, 2022 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> Anderson is a fan of Sandler's comedies, and said his love for his films became "obsession-level" after seeing and enjoying Sandler's 1999 film ''[[Big Daddy (1999 film)|Big Daddy]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barfield |first=Charles |date=May 3, 2018 |title=Throwback Thursday: Paul Thomas Anderson Has An "Obsession" With Adam Sandler's 'Big Daddy' |url=https://theplaylist.net/tbt-paul-thomas-anderson-sandler-20180503/ |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=The Playlist}}</ref><ref name="EbertInterview" /> He was determined to make a film with Sandler as a lead, saying, "He's always just made me laugh, he gets me, I wanted a piece of him."<ref name="CrazyLA" /> He specifically wrote ''Punch-Drunk Love'' with Sandler and [[Emily Watson]] in mind. Anderson had to convince producer [[JoAnne Sellar]], who was "befuddled" with his desire to cast Sandler, that he was the right person for the job.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zak |date=November 4, 2020 |title='Punch-Drunk Love' Producer Looks Back at Casting Adam Sandler: 'I Was Just Befuddled' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2020/11/punch-drunk-love-producer-casting-adam-sandler-befuddled-1234596860/ |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=[[IndieWire]]}}</ref> Anderson took inspiration for Barry Egan's characterization from watching the ''[[Saturday Night Live]]: The Best of Adam Sandler'' compilation DVD, primarily with the skit "[[The Denise Show]]",<ref name="LATimes">{{Cite web |last=Brownfield |first=Paul |date=November 5, 2000 |title=Speak Softly and Carry a Big Shtick |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-nov-05-ca-47189-story.html |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref><ref name="EbertInterview" /> saying,

{{Blockquote|text=I saw this ''Best of Adam Sandler'' DVD from ''Saturday Night Live'', and an amazing thing happened. There's this moment when he's doing this talk show called ''The Denise Show'', about his ex-girlfriend who's left him, and his father calls up and says, "What are you doing; you're embarrassing the family". And Adam goes into this fit of rage, screaming at his father, and honest to God I saw this moment where it appears as if the whites of his eyes turn black and they roll back in his head. It was like, he just lost his mind. I would play it back, over and over again, and you can see him kinda snap back to reality. The audience is laughing and it's almost like he finally started to hear them laughing a few seconds later.<ref name="EbertInterview" />}}

Anderson described the film as an "art-house Adam Sandler film", while film critic [[Roger Ebert]] felt Anderson "deconstructed the Adam Sandler movies and put them back together again in a new way at a different level".<ref name="EbertInterview">{{Cite web |last=Ebert |first=Roger |date=October 13, 2002 |title='Love' at first sight |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/interviews/love-at-first-sight |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=[[Rogerebert.com]]}}</ref> In writing the elements of the [[Healthy Choice]] frequent-flier miles sub-plot line, Anderson was inspired by the real-life story of [[David Phillips (entrepreneur)|David Phillips]], who successfully amassed over a million frequent flier miles from buying $3,000 worth of Healthy Choice's pudding. Anderson received approval from Phillips and Healthy Choice to adapt Phillips' story into the film.<ref name="usatoday2">{{Cite web|last = Puig|first = Claudia|title = The proof of 'Punch-Drunk Love' is in the pudding|publisher = [[USA Today]]|date = October 7, 2002|url = https://www.usatoday.com/life/movies/news/2002-10-07-pudding_x.htm|accessdate = 2011-02-26|archive-date = 2012-05-11|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120511190905/http://www.usatoday.com/life/movies/news/2002-10-07-pudding_x.htm|url-status = live}}</ref> A major source of inspiration for ''Punch-Drunk Love'' came from the films of [[Jacques Tati]], while Barry's blue suit was inspired by musicals, such as ''[[The Band Wagon]]'' (1953) and ''[[Singin' in the Rain]]'' (1952)''.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kehr |first=Dave |date=October 6, 2002 |title=FILM; A Poet of Love And Chaos In the Valley |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/10/06/movies/film-a-poet-of-love-and-chaos-in-the-valley.html |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

Filming and editing took place over a year and a half for several reasons, such as Anderson scrapping the first two weeks of shooting over fears that he was "making the same movie" as his previous filmography, as well as the threat of Hollywood strikes in 2001, that led to Sandler and Watson filming other projects in between filming ''Punch-Drunk Love''. Anderson declined more funding from [[Revolution Studios]], as he was determined to keep the film under $30 million in terms of budget.<ref name="CrazyLA" />

Anderson brought in the visual artist [[Jeremy Blake]] to create what ''[[The New York Times]]'' called "trippy, fluid sequences of abstract art" to use as transitions in the film.<ref>{{cite web| website=The New York Times| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/01/arts/design/01blake.html| title=Jeremy Blake, 35, Artist Who Used Lush-Toned Video, Dies| first=Randy| last=Kennedy| date=August 1, 2007| accessdate=October 3, 2024}}</ref>

=== Casting ===
Sandler shared phone numbers with [[Tom Cruise]] when he visited ''Saturday Night Live'' during the taping of an episode hosted by Cruise's then-wife [[Nicole Kidman]]. While filming ''Magnolia'', Anderson contacted Sandler through a phone call with Cruise and expressed his intention to write a film for him, and despite being unfamiliar with Anderson, Sandler gave his blessing. Sandler was intimidated upon first viewing ''Magnolia'', leading him to be "fucking terrified" and doubt his ability to carry Anderson's next film. Anderson helped alleviate Sandler's fears upon personally delivering the script.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zak |date=October 16, 2020 |title='Magnolia' Freaked Out Adam Sandler So Much He Nearly Turned Down 'Punch-Drunk Love' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2020/10/magnolia-freaked-out-adam-sandler-punch-drunk-love-1234593387/ |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=[[IndieWire]]}}</ref> Sandler's casting was officially announced in November 2000; the unconventional pairing shocked reporters as Anderson was a rising filmmaker noted for his critically acclaimed films, while Sandler was known for negatively-reviewed mainstream comedies.<ref name="LATimes" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 9, 2000 |title=Boogie Nights creator recruits Sandler |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2000/nov/09/news |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> [[Sean Penn]] was originally offered the role of Dean Trumbell, but turned it down and [[Philip Seymour Hoffman]] was cast instead.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-06 |title=Sean Penn Rediscovered His Love of Acting With 'One Battle After Another' |url=https://www.wmagazine.com/culture/sean-penn-cover-interview-one-battle-after-another |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=W Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

Aside from the primary named cast, all on-screen actors are non-professionals, which Anderson found more interesting and less complicated.<ref name="CrazyLA" />

===Music===
{{main|Punch-Drunk Love (soundtrack)}}

The score to ''Punch-Drunk Love'' was composed by [[Jon Brion]]. As with ''Magnolia'', Brion and Anderson collaborated heavily for the production of the film's score. However, rather than scoring the film after rough footage had been shot, Brion made compositions while the film was being made. During the scoring process, Brion would experiment with tones and sounds, carefully making note of what Anderson would respond to. Anderson would create the vocal tempos he would envision in the score and use them on set, even to the extent of inspiring the pace of Sandler's performance.

The film's score features no [[harmonium]] in the score outside of the notes Sandler plays on it.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seibold |first=Witney |date=2023-01-14 |title=How Adam Sandler Influenced The Soundtrack To Paul Thomas Anderson's Punch-Drunk Love |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1167382/how-adam-sandler-influenced-the-soundtrack-to-paul-thomas-andersons-punch-drunk-love/ |access-date=2024-12-10 |website=[[/Film|SlashFilm]]}}</ref> Brion introduced the instrument to Anderson during their work on ''Magnolia''; however, an article stating it was used heavily in the score is incorrect per Brion's account.<ref>{{cite web |last=Chapman |first=Glen |title=Music in the movies: Jon Brion |url=http://www.denofgeek.us/movies/17063/music-in-the-movies-jon-brion |website=[[Den of Geek]] |date=21 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151211022418/http://www.denofgeek.us/movies/17063/music-in-the-movies-jon-brion |archive-date=2015-12-11 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Many scenes between Sandler's character and the instrument were inspired by Brion. For instance, Brion once found a harmonium with a hole in its bellows, before going on tour with [[Aimee Mann]]. To fix the problem, he covered the hole with duct tape. The situation is mirrored in the film.

==Reception==
===Box office===
''Punch-Drunk Love'' began a limited domestic release on October 11, 2002, grossing $118,539 from five theaters. It had grossed $17.8 million in the United States, and an international total of $6.8 million, for a worldwide box office total of $24.6 million.<ref name="BOM" />

===Critical reception===
[[File:Adamsandler(cannesPhotocall).jpg|thumb|284x284px|[[Adam Sandler]]'s performance as Barry Egan received acclaim and surprised many critics due to it being a departure from his usual film roles. He received a [[Golden Globe Awards|Golden Globe Award]] nomination for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy|Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy]].]]
On [[review aggregator]] [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the film holds an approval rating of 79% based on 201 reviews. The website's critical consensus states, "Odd, touching, and unique, ''Punch-Drunk Love'' is also delightfully funny, utilizing Adam Sandler's comic persona to explore the life of a lonely guy who finds love."<ref>{{cite web |title=Punch-Drunk Love |work=Rotten Tomatoes |url=http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/punchdrunk_love/ |access-date=2025-03-07 |archive-date=2010-02-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100216183219/http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/punchdrunk_love/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the film has a [[weighted average]] score of 78 out of 100, based on 37 critics, indicating "generally favorable reviews".<ref>{{cite web |title=Punch-Drunk Love |work=Metacritic |url=http://www.metacritic.com/movie/punch-drunk-love |access-date=2014-08-18 |archive-date=2014-09-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140905050641/http://www.metacritic.com/movie/punch-drunk-love |url-status=live }}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "D+" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cinemascore |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220122629/https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |archive-date=2018-12-20}}</ref>

Writing for ''[[Rolling Stone]]'', [[Peter Travers]] felt the pairing of Anderson and Sandler was "parallel lines that meet triumphantly in a mesmerizer that stays true to both of their anarchic spirits," and praised the cast's performances, ultimately calling the film's effect "intoxicating."<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Travers |first=Peter |date=November 1, 2002 |title=Movie Review: Punch-Drunk Love |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-reviews/punch-drunk-love-248540/ |url-access=registration |access-date=April 20, 2022 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]}}</ref> Angie Errigo of ''[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]]'' complimented Anderson's direction as "simply captivating and exquisitely controlled, with a restless mood and no end of fascinating, beautifully-orchestrated oddness," and said, "One of the joys of this film...is that you really have no idea what's going to happen next."<ref name="EmpireReview">{{Cite web |last=Errigo |first=Angie |date=January 1, 2001 |title=Punch-Drunk Love Review |url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/reviews/punch-drunk-love-review/ |access-date=April 20, 2022 |website=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]}}</ref> Daniel Fierman of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' thought the film was a "meditation on true love, the ways in which we are all bizarre, the magic of the perfect match, and the preposterously unlikely nature of the whole enterprise."<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Fierman |first=Daniel |date=June 27, 2003 |title=Punch-Drunk Love |url=https://ew.com/article/2003/06/27/punch-drunk-love-4/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]}}</ref> The ''[[Los Angeles Times]]''<nowiki/>' [[Kenneth Turan]] stated that the film was "a comedy of discomfort and rage that turns unexpectedly sweet and pure."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Turan |first=Kenneth |date=October 11, 2002 |title=Isn't It Daringly, Absurdly Romantic? |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-oct-11-et-turan11-story.html |access-date=April 25, 2022 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', [[Todd McCarthy]] said that "there is no mistaking the exceeding creativity that has gone into nearly every shot, transition, narrative choice and musical selection," and praised Adam Sandler, Emily Watson, and [[Philip Seymour Hoffman]]'s performances. He also opined that "Sandler fans will probably take it as a lightweight, but agreeable enough, outing with slightly weird elements to it, while Anderson partisans could split between those who will revel in the thrill of his ongoing creative inventions and others who may find this light lifting between heavy workouts."<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCarthy |first=Todd |date=May 19, 2002 |title=Punch-Drunk Love |url=https://variety.com/2002/film/markets-festivals/punch-drunk-love-2-1200549551/ |access-date=January 29, 2024 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> Charles Taylor of ''[[Salon.com]]'' described the film as a "manic-depressive romantic comedy that aspires to the soul of a musical," and complimented Anderson's direction, [[Christopher Scarabosio]]'s sound design, and Jon Brion's score. He believed that Anderson properly utilized the "threat of sudden, bellowing, red-faced rage" of Sandler's known comic persona in the film.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Charles |date=October 11, 2002 |title=Love on the brink of chaos |url=https://www.salon.com/2002/10/11/punch_drunk/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Salon.com]]}}</ref>

[[David Ansen]] of ''[[Newsweek]]'' described the film as "a romantic comedy on the verge of a nervous breakdown," praising the film's unpredictability and cinematography, but felt Lena was underwritten, concluding that it was "an emotional jigsaw puzzle that's missing a couple of crucial pieces."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ansen |first=David |date=October 23, 2002 |title=Call Him Unhappy Gilmore |url=https://www.newsweek.com/call-him-unhappy-gilmore-146867 |access-date=April 20, 2022 |website=[[Newsweek]]}}</ref> Giving the film three stars out of five, [[Peter Bradshaw]] of ''[[The Guardian]]'' felt the story was "deeply unconvincing" and "a short cut to an entirely unearned emotional resolution that doesn't begin to illuminate the jagged and disturbing - and gripping - ideas that swirl around the beginning of this film," and felt the film's core romance was "the most bafflingly unreal love story you can imagine."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bradshaw |first=Peter |date=February 7, 2003 |title=Punch-Drunk Love |url=https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2003/feb/07/artsfeatures1 |access-date=May 29, 2022 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref>

Sandler's lead performance received acclaim. Giving the film three-and-a-half stars out of four, Roger Ebert of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' praised Sandler's performance in his review, saying, "Sandler, liberated from the constraints of formula, reveals unexpected depths as an actor. Watching this film, you can imagine him in [[Dennis Hopper]] roles. He has darkness, obsession and power. He can't go on making those moronic comedies forever, can he?"<ref>{{cite news |last=Ebert |first=Roger |date=October 18, 2002 |title=Punch-Drunk Love |publisher=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/punch-drunk-love-2002 |access-date=February 5, 2011 |archive-date=June 3, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603052539/http://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/punch-drunk-love-2002 |url-status=live }}</ref> Errigo called the film "an anti-Adam Sandler movie that proves to be a highly defining moment for the actor" and called Sandler's performance "astonishing." She also felt Watson was "relishing a calming character who is on an even keel."<ref name="EmpireReview" /> ''Entertainment Weekly''<nowiki/>'s [[Owen Gleiberman]] said Sandler was "utterly winning to watch" and added that "he has become a tender and arresting presence, like a fusion of [[Charlie Chaplin|Chaplin]]’s [[The Tramp|Little Tramp]], [[Woody Allen]], and [[Edward Scissorhands]]."<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Gleiberman |first=Owen |date=October 9, 2002 |title=Punch-Drunk Love |url=https://ew.com/article/2002/10/09/punch-drunk-love-2/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]}}</ref> [[Desson Thomson]] of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' proclaimed that Sandler gave "the performance of his life" in the film.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Howe |first=Desson |date=October 18, 2002 |title='Punch-Drunk'? Love It! |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/2002/10/18/punch-drunk-love-it/7991e1d0-d8c3-4833-8de3-f0012236d931/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=May 29, 2022 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref>

===Accolades===
Sandler went on to win Best Actor at the [[Gijón International Film Festival]] for his performance and was also nominated for the [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy]]. Anderson won the award for [[Best Director Award (Cannes Film Festival)|Best Director]] at the [[2002 Cannes Film Festival]] and the film was nominated for the [[Palme d'Or]].<ref name="festival-cannes.com">{{cite news |title=Festival de Cannes: Punch-Drunk Love |url=http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/3124026/year/2002.html |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120118145737/http://www.festival-cannes.com/en/archives/ficheFilm/id/3124026/year/2002.html |archive-date=January 18, 2012 |access-date=October 25, 2009 |publisher=Cannes Film Festival}}</ref> The film was nominated for the [[Grand Prix (Belgian Film Critics Association)|Grand Prix]] of the [[Belgian Film Critics Association|Belgian Syndicate of Cinema Critics]].

===Legacy===
''Punch-Drunk Love'' came in at #33 in ''[[The A.V. Club]]''{{'s}} "Top 50 films of the '00s",<ref name="The best films of the 00's">{{cite news |last1=Murray |first1=Noel |last2=Phipps |first2=Keith |last3=Rabin |first3=Nathan |last4=Robinson |first4=Tasha |last5=Tobias |first5=Scott |title=The best films of the 00's |publisher=[[The A.V. Club]] |url=https://www.avclub.com/the-best-films-of-the-00s-1798222348 |url-status=live |access-date=January 17, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100116094059/http://www.avclub.com/articles/the-best-films-of-the-00s%2C35931/2/ |archive-date=January 16, 2010}}</ref> while ''[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]]'' listed the film as one of the [[best films]] of the 21st century.<ref name="timeout.com">{{cite web |date=6 February 2022 |title=The 100 best films of the 21st century so far |url=https://www.timeout.com/film/the-100-best-movies-of-the-21st-century-so-far#:~:text=69.%C2%A0Punch%2DDrunk%20Love%20(2002) |website=[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]]}}</ref> In June 2025, the film ranked number 56 on ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century" and was one of the films voted for the "Readers' Choice" edition of the list, finishing at number 103.<ref>{{cite web |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |website=The New York Times |date=2 July 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/best-movies-21st-century.html | title=The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century | work=The New York Times | date=June 23, 2025 }}</ref> In July 2025, it ranked number 78 on ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century."<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-lists/best-movies-of-the-21st-century-1235200512/ | title=100 Best Movies of the 21st Century | magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] | date=July 1, 2025 }}</ref>

Filmmakers [[Francis Ford Coppola]], [[Lee Unkrich]], [[Judd Apatow]], [[Kleber Mendonça Filho|Kleber Mendonça]], [[Miranda July]], [[Bong Joon-ho]], [[David Gordon Green]], [[Guillermo del Toro]], [[Jason Reitman]], [[Isabel Sandoval]], [[Barry Jenkins]] and [[Taika Waititi]], and actors [[Brad Pitt]], [[Bill Nighy]], [[Owen Wilson]], [[Javier Bardem]], [[Daniel Day-Lewis]], [[Cillian Murphy]], [[Joseph Gordon-Levitt]], [[Austin Butler]], [[Guy Pearce]], [[Timothée Chalamet]], and [[Andrew Scott (actor)|Andrew Scott]] have cited it as one of their favorite films.<ref>{{cite web |last=Goodsell |first=Luke |date=June 15, 2010 |title=Five Favorite Films With ''Toy Story 3'' Director Lee Unkrich |url=http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/toy_story_3/news/1888943/five_favorite_films_with_toy_story_3_director_lee_unkrich/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100907192947/http://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/toy_story_3/news/1888943/five_favorite_films_with_toy_story_3_director_lee_unkrich/ |archive-date=September 7, 2010 |access-date=February 4, 2011 |publisher=Rotten Tomatoes}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Viera |first=Lauren |date=July 31, 2009 |title=Judd Apatow, king of the Funny People |work=Chicago Tribune |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2009/07/31/judd-apatow-king-of-the-funny-people/ |url-status=live |access-date=July 13, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130929000331/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2009-07-31/entertainment/0907300284_1_funny-people-judd-apatow-adam-sandler |archive-date=September 29, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Ordona |first=Michael |date=November 12, 2009 |title=Bill Nighy pretty much lived this role |work=Los Angeles Times |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2009-nov-12-et-performance12-story.html |url-status=live |access-date=July 13, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928110217/http://articles.latimes.com/2009/nov/12/entertainment/et-performance12 |archive-date=September 28, 2013}}</ref> The film was a major visual influence for the 2024 [[Pixar]] film ''[[Inside Out 2]]''.<ref name="Inside Out 2">{{cite web |last1=Anderton |first1=Ethan |date=April 17, 2024 |title=How Pixar's Inside Out 2 Took Surprising Inspiration From An Adam Sandler Movie |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1564343/how-pixar-inside-out-2-took-inspiration-adam-sandler-movie/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240422084346/https://www.slashfilm.com/1564343/how-pixar-inside-out-2-took-inspiration-adam-sandler-movie/ |archive-date=April 22, 2024 |access-date=May 8, 2024 |website=[[/Film]]}}</ref>

When asked about ''Punch-Drunk Love'' following its twentieth anniversary in 2022, Sandler said that the film enabled him to pursue films different from his usual roles, while sharing that it helped forge a close friendship between him and Anderson.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Connell |first=Sean |date=July 12, 2022 |title=How Adam Sandler Feels About Punch-Drunk Love As The Movie Turns 20 Years Old |url=https://www.cinemablend.com/interviews/how-adam-sandler-feels-about-punch-drunk-love-as-the-movie-turns-20-years-old |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=CinemaBlend}}</ref> The two reunited in their first project since ''Punch-Drunk Love'' when Anderson helped film segments of Sandler's [[Netflix]] comedy special ''100% Fresh'' (2018)''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gavin |first1=Hailey |date=October 17, 2018 |title=Paul Thomas Anderson Apparently Filmed Part of Adam Sandler's New Stand Up Special |url=https://slate.com/culture/2018/10/paul-thomas-anderson-adam-sandler-reunite-for-standup-special.html |access-date=December 9, 2018 |website=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]}}</ref>''

Critics agreed that ''Punch-Drunk Love'' remained as one of Sandler's best acting performances, and was a launchpad for Sandler to take on dramatic roles or opportunities outside of his usual mainstream comedies. In a retrospective review following its 2017 release on Netflix, ''[[GQ]]''<nowiki/>'s Miranda Popkey called the film "Adam Sandler's finest performance and P.T. Anderson's most underrated work," describing it as "a paean to love as a source of unfathomable power."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Popkey |first=Miranda |date=July 16, 2017 |title=Adam Sandler's Best Performance, Punch-Drunk Love, Is on Netflix Right Now |url=https://www.gq.com/story/best-adam-sandler-movie-is-now-on-netflix |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[GQ]]}}</ref> ''Far Out''<nowiki/>'s Arun Starkey described ''Punch-Drunk Love'' as Sandler's "first true foray into auteur cinema" and "the first indicator of his prowess as an actor and shows that if he is given a good enough script that isn't shackled by the tropes of a mainstream genre, he can actually do very well at carrying a three-dimensional character onto the big screen."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Starkey |first=Arun |date=September 9, 2021 |title=How 'Punch Drunk Love' hinted at Adam Sandler's acting credentials |url=https://faroutmagazine.co.uk/punch-drunk-love-adam-sandler-acting-credentials/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=Far Out}}</ref> Alan Dorich of ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' shared that the film's critical success "changed the course of Sandler's career forever" and "opened new opportunities that enhanced his legacy as a performer," leading to other dramatic roles in films such as ''[[Men, Women & Children (film)|Men, Women & Children]]'' (2014), ''[[The Meyerowitz Stories]]'' (2017), and ''[[Uncut Gems]]'' (2019).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dorich |first=Alan |date=August 21, 2022 |title=How Punch-Drunk Love Changed the Course of Adam Sandler's Career |url=https://www.cbr.com/punch-drunk-love-changed-adam-sandler-dramatic-career/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]]}}</ref>

==Home media==
The film was released on VHS and DVD by [[Sony Pictures Home Entertainment|Columbia TriStar Home Entertainment]] on June 24, 2003.

[[The Criterion Collection]] released the film on Blu-ray in November 2016 with a restored HD transfer, the first time the company had done so for Anderson and Sandler. It has behind-the-scenes featurette about a recording session for the film's soundtrack, a [[Cannes Film Festival|Cannes]] press conference and deleted scenes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Punch-Drunk Love |website=The Criterion Collection |url=https://www.criterion.com/films/27916-punch-drunk-love |access-date=2018-10-11 |archive-date=2018-10-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181011214613/https://www.criterion.com/films/27916-punch-drunk-love |url-status=live }}</ref>
